correctness.rationale: Isolated points are dense in a countable compact metric space by Baire, and each is on the dense orbit. That orbit has no repetition. For y in X′, there are distinct isolated orbit points tending to y, whose images are distinct by nonrepetition; their limit Ty is therefore nonisolated. This suffices for derivative invariance, without needing to assume that the images are isolated. In fact each orbit point is isolated: the preimage under the corresponding iterate of any later isolated point is an open set meeting the dense orbit at only that earlier point. A lower-rank cycle Q would have a clopen neighborhood U with U∩X′=Q. Since Q maps into U, the set of points in U that map into its clopen complement is compact and disjoint from X′, hence finite. The dense nonrepeating orbit visits infinitely many isolated points on each side of U, requiring infinitely many distinct exits, a contradiction. Recurrence forces every positive atom of an invariant probability to be periodic, leaving exactly the simplex of mixtures of the two fixed Diracs. Empirical limits are invariant by telescoping, and compactness and vanishing successive jumps force a connected nonempty cluster set, hence a unique closed interval in the mixture parameter. In the construction for a<b, each new run crosses its interior target with error at most the final length reciprocal; the target gap is bounded away from zero, so each run's length tends to infinity. Hence the prefix zero frequency has liminf a and limsup b. The quadratic paired lengths give singleton frequencies, including 0 and 1 by using a linear minority run. Diverging runs imply that every limit of distinct shifts has at most one change, and each one-change sequence and each constant is obtained by choosing starting positions in late runs. A prefix with two changes appears only at finitely many positions; since there is no periodic tail, each such shift can be isolated by a longer prefix. This proves precisely the asserted derivatives, countability and ordinal type. The o(N) changes imply that outside o(N) starting positions, every fixed observation window is constant, giving the required weak-star comparison to the zero-frequency mixture. No surjectivity is needed.
residual_risks: The finite arithmetic checks certify neither the infinite rank calculation nor the continuum of intervals. Those follow from the run limit and frequency arguments.

value.rationale: The result isolates a natural statistical invariant of dense-orbit systems. It makes the possible variation exact on a fixed countable compact type while leaving the entire invariant probability simplex fixed. It includes genericity for either endpoint or any mixture, true interval-valued historic behavior, and the maximal interval, rather than only one example of nonconvergence.
residual_risks: The maps vary with the prescribed interval. The statement does not classify surjective realizations or larger or permuted top derivatives.
